mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates reduce the cost of capital for corporations, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts and retail sales indicate robust consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST and RSAFS both rising) fails to produce positive 60d returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production below 100 (index base 2017=100) indicates supply constraints that increase input costs and reduce corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts signal a strengthening real estate market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST is rising.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 255.0) signals potential Federal Reserve tightening, which increases discount rates and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 255.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS) and fall in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling) fails to produce positive 60d returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investment and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is rising (by more than 0.25pp in the last month).
